trans-unit.source:
%1 basics

%1 makes it much harder to trace where your DFCN came from. It mixes your coins with the coins of other DeFCoN users in shared transactions. Your coins never leave your wallet, and only you can spend them.

How it works
  1. Your wallet splits part of your balance into standard amounts of slightly more than 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 DFCN, for example 10.0001 DFCN. Everyone uses the same amounts, so the coins look alike.
  2. For one of these amounts, your wallet joins a mixing session that is waiting at a masternode, or asks a randomly chosen masternode to start a new one.
  3. When at least %2 participants have joined, the masternode combines their coins into one transaction. Each wallet checks and signs only its own part, and gets the same amounts back to new addresses of its own.
  4. Each completed session is one round. Your wallet repeats this several times. You can set the number of rounds and the target balance in Options.
  5. Mixing runs in the background while the wallet is open. When you send from your %1 balance, your coins are already mixed.
Good to know
  • Staking: coins of exactly a standard amount, or of one of the larger amounts below, do not earn staking rewards, whether they are mixed or not, and staking never combines them or the mixing collaterals with your other coins. The target balance in Options sets roughly how much is mixed in the standard amounts.
  • Fees: mixing transactions are free. Creating the standard amounts costs a normal small network fee. Now and then a tiny collateral of about 0.0001 DFCN goes to the network to prevent abuse.
  • Privacy: the masternode running a session sees which coins take part in it, and the other participants are not guaranteed to be different people. More rounds make your coins harder to follow. Sending many mixed coins together in one payment can link them again.
  • Encrypted wallet: if the wallet is locked when you start mixing, it asks for your passphrase and unlocks for mixing only, so sending still needs the passphrase.
  • Backups: each round uses up to 9 new addresses. %1 needs automatic wallet backups to be switched on; they are on by default.

trans-unit.source:
Larger amounts

For larger sums there are three more amounts: 100.001, 1000.01 and 10000.1 DFCN. Your wallet mixes coins of these amounts, but it does not make them. You make them with one normal payment to yourself. Use this recipe only in a wallet whose receiving and change addresses are its own spendable P2PKH addresses, as they are by default: a wallet that was given other active descriptors may not recognise the coins it pays to itself.

  1. Create a new receiving address for each coin you want, and one more.
  2. On the Send page, add a recipient for each of these addresses. Pay exactly 100.001, 1000.01 or 10000.1 DFCN to each coin's address and 0.01 DFCN to the last one, with "Subtract fee from amount" switched off for every recipient.

%1 From then on, while mixing is switched on, your wallet mixes every coin of these amounts that it holds on such an address, whatever the target balance is. To keep a coin out, lock it before you start mixing: enable the coin control features in Options, then use Inputs… on the Send page.

  • The 0.01 DFCN is ordinary money for the mixing collaterals of these amounts. If your wallet has no ordinary, unmixed balance left for them, mixing these amounts can wait.
  • A normal payment can spend these coins like any other coin, mixed or not. Lock the ones you want to keep before you start mixing, or choose the coins of the payment yourself. While mixing is running, choose coins that are not of a standard or a larger amount, and neither lock nor spend a coin of these amounts that is waiting to be mixed until its session has ended: a session that loses its coin can cost a collateral.
  • A session needs other wallets that mix the same amount at the same time, so a larger amount can wait longer for its rounds.

trans-unit.source:
How much to mix

The standard amounts are at most about 10 DFCN, so on their own they suit smaller sums. The target balance in Options goes up to 10,000 DFCN, which already means a thousand mixed coins or more, and a payment can hold only so many coins: one payment from coins of the standard amounts can be at most about 6,700 DFCN. For more, use the larger amounts.

A payment from your %1 balance has no change. The mixed coins have to add up to the amount you send; what is left over goes to the fee, and the fee can be at most 0.1 DFCN by default. With coins of the larger amounts, switch off "Subtract fee from amount" for every recipient and send a little less than the coins add up to: the difference is the fee, so it has to cover the normal network fee and stay within the wallet's fee limit. Or keep coins of the standard amounts to make up the rest.
